Euphoria

yoo-FOR-ee-uh -- four syllables, stress on the second syllable, FOR. · noun

Hear It

What It Means

Euphoria is a feeling of intense excitement and happiness.

A wave of euphoria swept through mission control when the rover's signal finally returned.

Worked Example

She crosses the marathon's finish line, and for ten dizzy minutes the soreness simply does not exist -- she is laughing, hugging strangers, floating somewhere above the pavement.

That flood of feeling is euphoria: intense excitement and happiness, usually brief and overwhelming while it lasts. Euphoria is the peak itself -- higher than being elated, and far too intense to be anyone's everyday mood.

How Euphoria Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

delight

delight: great pleasure and joy

rapture

rapture: overwhelming joy that carries you away

Antonyms

despair

despair: the complete loss of hope

misery

misery: great unhappiness or suffering

How Strong Is It? — delight → euphoria → rapture

delight vs. euphoria

delight vs. euphoria: Delight is the gentle, weaker cousin -- a good dessert brings delight -- while euphoria is a tidal wave: happiness so intense it briefly crowds out everything else.

rapture vs. euphoria

rapture vs. euphoria: Rapture is euphoria's equal and closest twin: both name overwhelming joy, but rapture suggests being carried away and absorbed, while euphoria emphasizes the racing, electric high itself.

Build the Word

The pieces

prefix — eu-

prefix — eu-: good, well (Greek)

root — phor-

root — phor-: to bear, to carry (Greek pherein)

suffix — -ia

suffix — -ia: state or condition of (Greek)

Put it together

Put it together: Euphoria is Greek for 'bearing well' -- eu- ('good, well') plus pherein ('to carry'). Doctors once used it for a patient carrying an illness comfortably; today it names the state of being carried high by intense excitement and happiness.

Use the root in a new word: euphemism

Use the root in a new word: euphemism: Saying the hamster 'went to live on a farm' was Dad's favorite euphemism.

Root Check

Word Choice

Euphoria is a noun for the peak itself, and it rarely lasts: a wave of euphoria, the euphoria faded. Elated is the adjective for a person riding a high; euphoria is the high. If the feeling is quiet or long-lasting, reach for contentment instead -- euphoria always races.
